title: The Prisoners in the Cave
paragraphs: More than two thousand years ago, the Greek thinker Plato told a story about a cave. In the story, some people have lived in the cave since they were children. They cannot turn their heads, so they can only look at the wall in front of them.

Behind them, there is a fire, and people carry objects past it. The fire makes shadows on the wall, and the prisoners think that these shadows are real. One day, one prisoner is freed and walks outside. At first, the bright sun hurts his eyes, but slowly he sees the real world.

He returns to the cave to tell the others the truth. But they do not believe him, because the shadows are all they have ever known. Plato used the story to show how hard it can be to change what we think is true.

sources.claim: Platon'un Devlet'inde (Kitap VII) mağara alegorisi: çocukluktan beri zincirli mahkûmlar duvardaki gölgeleri gerçek sanır; serbest kalan biri güneşe çıkar, dönüp anlattığında diğerleri ona inanmaz.
